newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada advance team to Zaire waits in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Canada advance team to Zaire waits in Kenya.

text.p: An advance team of 24 Canadian soldiers was in Kenya on Saturday awaiting clearance to enter Rwanda as part of a multinational mission in aid of Rwandan refugees in Zaire, Canadian officials said.

The soldiers are the first wave of a larger Canadian reconnaissance contingent heading for eastern Zaire. They must get Rwandan government approval before crossing into Rwanda, Canadian military officials said.

"The reconnaissance team is still in Nairobi, Kenya, awaiting clearance to go to Kigali, Rwanda. The decision is in Rwanda's hands," Capt. Michel Arsenault told Reuters from the Department of National Defence headquarters in Ottawa.

The U.N. Security Council gave final approval on Friday for the deployment of a Canadian-led multinational force to bring humanitarian assistance to primarily Hutu Rwandan refugees stranded in eastern Zaire by fighting between Zairean forces and Tutsi rebels.
The multinational force's commander, Canadian Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril, was to spend much of the weekend planning the mission.
Canadian officials were not able to provide details on Saturday of when the first wave of Canadian soldiers, aside from the reconnaissance personnel, would begin arriving in Zaire.

They said three Hercules C-130 transport aircraft carrying equipment and light vehicles were scheduled to leave the Canadian military base in Trenton, Ontario, on Saturday bound for Zaire. An additional 120 reconnaissance personnel were scheduled to leave Trenton on an Airbus jet on Sunday afternoon.
Canadian military officials said it would take between 30 to 35 hours for the propeller-driven Hercules planes to reach their destinations, while the Airbus flight would be faster.
At the Trenton base, Capt. Ian Stock said the departure of the 120 reconnaissance personnel had been delayed until Sunday afternoon so the soldiers would not reach Zaire ahead of their equipment.

Canadian officials said the movement of thousands of refugees back into Rwanda from Zaire on Friday and on Saturday had not changed plans for the deployment of the multinational humanitarian aid force.

On Friday, Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said a strong international presence was still needed in Zaire. "I don't think you want to dilute your efforts in any way now," he said, noting that airports in eastern Zaire needed to be secured and safe corridors provided for the hundreds of thousands of refugees remaining.
